design_contract.O1-F1: All principal operationalization choices are fixed, and the bounded finding roles are explicit.
design_contract.O1-F2: The effective operationalization is identical to O1-F1, while the participant selects the principal findings without an exhaustive fixed checklist.
design_contract.O2-F1: Exactly one or two principal operationalization dimensions remain open; all other choices and bounded findings stay explicit.
design_contract.O3-F1: All principal operationalization dimensions remain participant-selected; the target, scope, and bounded finding roles stay fixed.

questions.blunt_fin_o1_f1: Examine the blunt-fin flow field and determine which high-speed flow region is strongest. At each location, define speed as the magnitude of the velocity vector. From all non-zero speed values, compute q90, the 90th-percentile cutoff, and retain locations whose speed is greater than or equal to q90. Partition the retained locations into regions using face connectivity. For each region, record its peak speed; select the region with the largest peak, and report that peak speed together with the mean spatial position of the region’s retained locations.
questions.blunt_fin_o1_f2: Using the blunt-fin flow field, investigate the strongest high-speed region. Define speed by velocity magnitude, retain values at or above the 90th percentile of non-zero recorded speed, and combine face-connected retained locations into individual regions. Use peak speed to select the strongest region and the mean spatial location of its retained locations to place it. Report the principal findings that you consider scientifically relevant, supported by evidence; these should include the region’s defining strength and location as well as at least one further characterization of your choice.
questions.blunt_fin_o2_f1: Identify the strongest high-speed region in the flow around the blunt fin. Use velocity magnitude as the flow quantity, group face-connected retained locations into one region, and represent each region by the mean spatial location of those locations. You should choose and state a scientifically appropriate rule for deciding which locations are high-speed and a measure for comparing region strength, then report the selected region’s location and strength.
questions.blunt_fin_o3_f1: Investigate high-speed flow regions in the blunt-fin dataset and decide which one is strongest. Choose and explain how the field will be represented or aggregated, what will count as a high-speed region, the criterion used to select locations, and the property used to compare region strength. Apply that operationalization and report the location and strength of the strongest region.
questions.carotid_o1_f1: Which high-speed flow region is strongest in the carotid artery dataset? Compute speed as the Euclidean magnitude of the velocity vector, classify non-zero speeds at or above their 90th percentile as high-speed, and form regions from face-connected qualifying locations. Select the region with the greatest peak speed, and give both that peak value and the mean spatial location of the retained locations within the region.
questions.carotid_o1_f2: Study the carotid artery flow field to identify its strongest high-speed region. At each location, use the Euclidean magnitude of the available velocity vector as speed; retain values at or above the 90th percentile of non-zero speed; and treat face-connected retained locations as one region. Rank the resulting regions by peak speed and locate the selected region using the mean position of its retained locations. Present the principal evidence-supported findings you judge important, including the selected region’s strength and location and at least one additional scientifically relevant characterization of your choice.
questions.carotid_o2_f1: Determine which high-speed region is strongest in the carotid artery flow. Calculate speed from the Euclidean magnitude of velocity and combine face-connected qualifying locations into contiguous regions whose locations are summarized by the mean position of their retained points. Select and state a scientifically defensible high-speed criterion and a regional strength measure, then report the strongest region’s location and strength under those choices.
questions.carotid_o3_f1: How would you operationalize the search for the strongest high-speed region in the carotid artery flow field? Decide how to represent or aggregate the flow, how a high-speed region is defined, which selection criterion to apply, and how region strength is measured. Use your choices to identify the strongest region and report where it is and how strong it is.
questions.combustor_density_level_set_surface_prov: Find a scientifically relevant coherent constant-density structure in the annular-combustor flow field. Construct the constant-Density isosurface at the 90th percentile of the finite stored Density values, treat each connected surface component as a candidate, and select the component with the largest surface area. Represent the selected surface by its area-weighted centroid and surface area, and report its centroid location, defining density value, and surface extent.

Explore coherent constant-density structure in the annular-combustor flow by extracting the Density isosurface at the 90th percentile of finite stored values. Consider every connected isosurface component as a candidate, select the one with the largest surface area, and describe it using its area-weighted centroid and surface area. Report the principal findings that the data support, including the structure’s identity and defining density level, along with a scientifically relevant characterization of your choice concerning its extent, location, or shape.

In the annular-combustor flow field, identify one scientifically relevant coherent constant-density structure. Choose and state a rule for setting the Density isovalue from the finite stored Density values. At that level, treat each connected isosurface component as a candidate, select the component with the largest surface area, and represent it by its area-weighted centroid and surface area. Report the selected structure’s centroid, Density isovalue, and surface area.

Investigate the annular-combustor flow field for a coherent constant-density spatial structure that is scientifically relevant. You should decide how such a structure is defined, how one candidate is selected, and what spatial representation or aggregation is used to characterize it. Report the resulting structure’s representative location, defining density value, and spatial extent.
questions.fireflow_o1_f1: Locate the strongest contiguous high-speed flow region in the FireFlow room dataset. Use velocity magnitude, retain locations whose non-zero recorded speeds fall at or above the 90th percentile, and merge mesh-connected retained locations into a region. Take peak speed as regional strength, and report both the peak speed of the strongest region and the mean spatial location of its retained high-speed locations.
questions.fireflow_o1_f2: Analyze the FireFlow room to determine the strongest high-speed flow region. Treat velocity magnitude values at or above the 90th percentile of non-zero recorded speed as high-speed, form regions from mesh-connected qualifying locations, use peak speed to compare them, and represent the selected region by the mean position of its retained locations. Select and report the principal scientifically relevant findings supported by the evidence, including the region’s strength and location and at least one further characterization that you consider informative.
questions.fireflow_o2_f1: Within the FireFlow room flow field, find the strongest high-speed region. Use velocity magnitude, treat mesh-connected retained locations as a single region, and summarize its position by the mean spatial location of those retained locations. Choose a scientifically appropriate high-speed criterion and a measure of regional strength, state both choices, and report the selected region’s location and strength.
questions.fireflow_o3_f1: Develop a suitable analysis for identifying the strongest high-speed flow region in the FireFlow room. Select the flow representation or aggregation, define what constitutes a high-speed region, decide on a selection criterion, and choose how its strength will be measured. Then apply your method and report the location and strength of the region you identify as strongest.
questions.kitchen_concentration_heterogeneity_o1_f: Among the gas-concentration fields in the kitchen airflow, which field is most spatially heterogeneous? Treat the point-associated fields c1 and c11–c17 as separate candidates. For each candidate, first compute the arithmetic mean of its finite vertex values in each cell, ignore cells with non-positive volume, and then calculate the coefficient of variation using cell volume as the weight. Select the field with the largest value and report its identifier and coefficient of variation.

Compare the point-associated gas-concentration fields c1 and c11–c17 in the kitchen airflow. For each field, first compute the arithmetic mean of its finite vertex values in each cell, ignore cells with non-positive volume, and then calculate the coefficient of variation using cell volume as the weight. Report evidence for the selected field and its heterogeneity measure, together with at least one additional scientifically relevant characterization of the result.
questions.kitchen_concentration_heterogeneity_o2_f: Assess spatial heterogeneity across all available gas-concentration fields in the kitchen airflow data. Treat every stored gas-concentration field as a candidate, but choose and state the scientifically appropriate heterogeneity measure used to compare them. Identify the field with the greatest value under your measure, and report both the selected field and that value.
questions.kitchen_concentration_heterogeneity_o3_f: Which available gas-concentration field in the kitchen airflow is most spatially heterogeneous under a scientifically appropriate analysis of your choice? Decide how the fields should be represented, what spatial feature will define heterogeneity, and which property measure will be used for comparison. Apply those choices and report the field you select and its resulting heterogeneity value.
questions.nasa_lox_post_o1_f1: Determine the strongest high-speed flow region in the NASA LOx-post dataset. Use velocity magnitude as speed, keep locations at or above the 90th percentile of non-zero recorded speed, and treat face-connected retained locations as a single region. Compare regions by peak speed and locate the selected region by the mean position of its retained locations; report both the location and peak strength.
questions.nasa_lox_post_o1_f2: In the NASA LOx-post flow field, use velocity magnitude to define speed and retain locations at or above the 90th percentile of non-zero recorded values. Build regions from face-connected retained locations, select the strongest one by peak speed, and use the mean spatial position of its retained locations as its representative location. From this fixed analysis, report the principal findings you consider scientifically significant, supported by evidence; include strength and location evidence and at least one further characterization of your choice.
questions.nasa_lox_post_o2_f1: Identify the strongest high-speed region in the NASA LOx-post flow field. Use the supplied velocity vectors to compute speed as their magnitude, treat face-connected retained locations as a single region, and represent the selected region by the mean spatial location of its retained locations. Choose and state both a scientifically appropriate criterion for retaining high-speed locations and a property measure for comparing region strength, then report the strongest region’s location and strength.
questions.nasa_lox_post_o3_f1: Examine the NASA LOx-post flow field and construct an analysis that identifies its strongest high-speed region. Choose how the field is represented or aggregated, define what qualifies as a high-speed region, set an appropriate selection criterion, and decide how regional strength is measured. Use the resulting operationalization to report the strongest region’s location and strength.
questions.office_speed_zones_o1_f1: In the office ventilation flow, identify the strongest contiguous high-speed region. Define speed as velocity magnitude, retain locations where it is above 0.20 in the stored velocity scale, and regard locations connected through shared grid faces as one region. Use peak speed to compare regions, represent the selected region by the mean spatial location of its retained locations, and report its location and peak strength.
questions.office_speed_zones_o1_f2: Investigate high-speed ventilation in the office by retaining velocity-magnitude values above 0.20 in the stored scale and grouping face-connected retained locations into individual regions. Select the strongest region using peak speed and locate it by the mean spatial position of its retained locations. Report the principal scientifically relevant findings supported by the analysis, including evidence for the selected region’s strength and location and at least one additional characterization of your choice.
questions.office_speed_zones_o2_f1: Which high-speed ventilation region is strongest in the office velocity field under a scientifically defensible analysis? Use velocity magnitude, treat face-connected retained locations as one region, and represent each region by the mean spatial location of those locations. Choose and state the high-speed criterion and the property measure used to compare region strength, then report the location and strength of the selected region.
questions.office_speed_zones_o3_f1: Design and apply an analysis to find the strongest high-speed ventilation region in the office flow field. Decide how to represent or aggregate the flow, how the region feature is defined, which criterion identifies high-speed locations, and which measure determines regional strength. Report where the strongest region is located and the strength assigned to it by your analysis.
